title: The History of the Pencil V1

parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: The History of the Pencil
parts.article:
The History of Pencil
 
(A) The beginning of the story of pencils started with a lightning. Graphite, the main material for producing pencil, was discovered in 1564 in Borrowdale in England when a lightning struck a local tree during a thunder. Local people found out that the black substance spotted at the root of the unlucky tree was different from burning ash of wood. It was soft, thus left marks everywhere. Chemistry was barely out of its infancy at the time, so people mistook it for lead, equally black but much heavier. It was soon put to use by locals in marking their sheep for ownership and calculation.
 
(B) Britain turns out to be major country where mines of graphite can be detected and developed. Even so, the first pencil was invented elsewhere. As graphite is soft, it requires some form of encasement. In Italy, graphite sticks were initially wrapped in string or sheepskin for stability, becoming perhaps the very first pencil in the world. Then around 1560, an Italian couple made what are likely the first blueprints for the modern, wood-encased carpentry pencil. Their version was a flat, oval, more compact type of pencil. Their concept involved the hollowing out of a stick of juniper wood. Shortly thereafter in 1662, a superior technique was discovered by German people: two wooden halves were carved, a graphite stick inserted, and the halves then glued together - essentially the same method in use to this day. The news of the usefulness of these early pencils spread far and wide, attracting the attention of artists all over the known world.
 
(C) Although graphite core in pencils is still referred to as lead, modern pencils do not contain lead as the “lead” of the pencil is actually a mix of finely ground graphite and clay powders. This mixture is important because the amount of clay content added to the graphite depends on the intended pencil hardness, and the amount of time spent on grinding the mixture determines the quality of the lead. The more clay you put in, the higher hardness the core has. Many pencils across the world, and almost all in Europe, are graded on the European system. This system of naming used B for black and H for hard; a pencil’s grade was described by a sequence or successive Hs or Bs such as BB and BBB for successively softer leads, and HH and HHH for successively harder ones. Then the standard writing pencil is graded HB.
 
(D) In England, pencils continue to be made from whole sawn graphite. But with the mass production of pencils, they are getting drastically more popular in many countries with each passing decade. As demands rise, appetite for graphite soars.
 
(E) According to the United States Geological Survey (USGS), world production of natural graphite in 2012 was 1,100,000 tonnes, of which the following major exporters are: China, India, Brazil, North Korea and Canada. However, much in contrast with its intellectual application in producing pencils, graphite was also widely used in the military. During the reign of Elizabeth I, Borrowdale graphite was used as a refractory material to line moulds for cannonballs, resulting in rounder, smoother balls that could be fired farther, contributing to the strength of the English navy. This particular deposit of graphite was extremely pure and soft, and could easily be broken into sticks. Because of its military importance, this unique mine and its production were strictly controlled by the Crown.
 
(F) That the United States did not use pencils in the outer space till they spent $1000 to make a pencil to use in zero gravity conditions is in fact a fiction. It is widely known that astronauts in Russia used grease pencils, which don’t have breakage problem. But it is also a fact that their counterparts in the United States used pencils in the outer space before real zero gravity pencil was invented. They preferred mechanical pencils, which produced fine line, much clearer than the smudgy lines left by the grease pencils that Russians favored. But the lead tips of these mechanical pencils broke often. That bit of graphite floating around the space capsule could get into someone’s eye, or even find its way into machinery or electronics, causing an electrical short or other problems. But despite the fact that the Americans did invent zero gravity pencils later, they stuck to mechanical pencils for many years.
 
(G) Against the backcloth of a digitalized world, the prospect of pencils seems bleak. In reality, it does not. The application of pencils has by now become so widespread that they can be seen everywhere, such as classrooms, meeting rooms and art rooms, etc. A spectrum of users are likely to continue to use it into the future: students to do math works, artists to draw on sketch pads, waiters or waitresses to mark on order boards, make-up professionals to apply to faces, and architects to produce blue prints. The possibilities seem limitless.

groups.contentHtml:
The early history of graphite in Britain
• Graphite was first found below a blown down in a storm.
• The first use of graphite was to make marks on .
• The characteristics of raw graphite:
  – dirty to use because it is so .
  – originally wrapped in or animal skin to make it useable as a pencil.
• Graphite came to the notice of the government for military and commercial purposes.
  – The government completely took over the at Borrowdale.
  – They employed guards to protect the graphite on its journey south.
• Local people began to graphite for the money involved.
  – The government passed a law to protect the graphite industry.

analyses.content: 你可能会想填村庄或地点，但题目问的是在什么东西“下面（below）”发现的，原文明确说是“在树下面（Underneath the tree）”。

When some particularly ferocious weather struck the Lake District in North West England in the sixteenth century, locals in the village of Borrowdale discovered a large uprooted tree. Underneath the tree lay an unknown black substance which we now know as graphite, was slightly shiny and smooth to the touch.
原文说在暴风雨吹倒的一棵大树下面发现了石墨，因此填 tree。
原文提到当地农民最初用这种新发现的材料来标记他们的羊，所以填 sheep。
你可能会看到下一句的 paper，但这只是别人后来发现的潜力，不是“最初的用途（first use）”。

(B) Initially, the local farmers used the newly discovered material as a handy way to identify their sheep. However, others quickly realised the potential for using this intriguing substance to write on paper.
原文说这种材料未经处理时非常软（soft），导致处理起来很脏（messy），对应题目中的 dirty。
你可能想填 untreated（未经处理的），但题目问的是导致它脏的具体特征，原文的逻辑是“因为软，所以脏”。
When it was untreated the material was very soft, which meant that it was messy to handle.
你可能会因为题目里有 animal skin 就不知道填什么，其实原文的 sheep hides 就对应动物皮，剩下的并列项就是 rope。
原文说人们把石墨包裹在坚硬的羊皮（animal skin的同义替换）或绳子（rope）里来方便使用。
To make it fit for use with paper, people enclosed a thin core of the substance in stiff sheep hides or rope.
原文指出政府意识到石墨的商业潜力，便控制了 Borrowdale 的所有矿（mines）。
你可能会想填 graphite（石墨），但这与前面的 the 重复且不符合“接管某个地点/设施”的语境，接管的是矿区。

In addition to its value to the armed forces, the government quickly realised the commercial potential of the graphite at Borrowdale, and assumed control of all the mines there during the sixteenth century.
原文提到石墨太值钱了，以至于当地人开始偷（steal）它。
你可能会寻找和 money 直接对应的词，但原文用 valuable（有价值的）替换了 money，说明了偷窃的动机。
The graphite was so valuable that the locals, who called it wad, started to steal it.

groups.description:
Complete the notes below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 1–6 on your answer sheet.

questions.question: The Italians were the first to make pencils out of wood.

analyses.content: (D) The Italians originally invented the wooden casing to hold a thin rod of plumbago firmly in place for ease of writing.
你可能会怀疑 originally 不是 first，但在这种语境下“最初发明”就等同于“第一个做”。
原文明确说意大利人“最初发明了（originally invented）”木制外壳来固定石墨，也就是最早用木头做铅笔，表述一致。

questions.question: The Germans used different types of wood to produce pencils.

analyses.content: 原文只提到德国人应用了大规模生产技术来进一步发展铅笔，根本没提他们用了“不同种类的木头”。
你可能会看到上文意大利人用了雪松木（cedar wood），就脑补德国人肯定换了别的木头，但文章没写就是没写，不能靠常识瞎猜。

Italian craftsmen hollowed out two small sections of cedar wood, into one of which they laid the lead. They then glued the other section over the top and left the two halves to set. When dry, the whole apparatus formed what today we know as a pencil. The Germans took this technique and developed it further by applying mass-production techniques to pencils.

questions.question: More clay in a pencil makes it write more darkly.

analyses.content: 原文说加更多的黏土会让铅笔更硬、更尖、更精准，而加更多石墨才会变得更黑（darker），题目把黏土和石墨的作用弄反了。
你可能会把“clay（黏土）”和“graphite（石墨）”的作用张冠李戴，做题时一定要看清是哪种材料导致了 darker。
Adding more clay to the mixture helped make the pencil harder, sharper, and more precise in its mark. More graphite helped make a pencil mark that was softer, thicker and darker.

questions.question: After the HB code was introduced, it very quickly became used by all manufacturers.

analyses.content: (E) The varying quality of pencil leads eventually gave rise to a system for categorizing the fineness of the pencil mark. Pencil manufacturers all over the world still use this so-called HB grading system today.
原文只说全世界的制造商“至今仍在使用”这个系统，但完全没有提到这个系统在推出后是否“非常快（very quickly）”被所有人使用。
你可能会看到“all over the world（全世界）”就觉得这代表普及得很快，但“范围广”和“时间快”是完全不同的两个概念。

questions.question: English pencil factories have now all closed down.

analyses.content: 原文明确说英格兰的铅笔工业在附近的 Keswick 镇“继续繁荣发展（continues to thrive）”，并没有全部倒闭。
你可能会看到前半句说 Borrowdale 的高级石墨“已经枯竭（totally exhausted）”，就误以为工厂也全关门了。
Nowadays the highest grade of graphite at Borrowdale is totally exhausted, although other grades can still be found, and England’s pencil industry continues to thrive in the nearby town of Keswick.

questions.question: American astronauts used pencils on their early journeys into space.

analyses.content: 原文澄清了事实，说美国和俄罗斯的宇航员在最初的太空飞行中“都配备了铅笔”。
你可能会被前面的谣言（美国人花几百万发明太空笔）误导，一定要往后读到“In actual fact”这句真正的结论。

It should be pointed out though, that the popular myth about Americans overlooking the practical advantages of pencils in zero gravity is merely fiction. In actual fact, both American and Russian astronauts were equipped with pencils in their respective countries’ first space flights.

questions.question: The use of graphite pencils is unlikely to continue into the future.

analyses.content: 原文说没有任何迹象表明我们会发明出比石墨更好的东西来做铅笔，意思是石墨铅笔在未来还会继续被使用，与题目的 unlikely 相反。
你可能会看到高科技时代（high-tech times）就以为铅笔要被淘汰了，但作者在最后一段的态度是铅笔极具韧性，会一直用下去。

But no matter — pencils remain in use in every classroom, every planning, building and drawing office, and in every art studio in the world. And there is nothing to suggest that we are likely to invent anything better than graphite to use in our pencils.
